title: Privacy notice linked from the home page
question: Can a visitor reach a privacy notice from the home page, and does it name who is responsible?
method: Find the home-page link whose label names privacy in the page language (privacy, Datenschutz, confidentialité, privacidad, privacidade, riservatezza, tratamiento de datos) and read the page. Found when it answers with 200 and names a controller or company with a contact (an email address or a postal address); review when the page exists but names no one; not found when no privacy link is on the home page.

spec.title: California Online Privacy Protection Act, Bus. & Prof. Code §22577(b)

title: Privacy contact published
question: Does the privacy notice name a data protection officer or privacy officer with a way to reach them?
method: In the privacy notice, look for a named role (data protection officer, DPO, Datenschutzbeauftragter, délégué à la protection des données, encarregado, responsable de la protection des renseignements personnels, privacy officer) followed within a short distance by an email address. Found when both are present; review when the role is named without a contact, or a privacy email is given without a role; not found otherwise. Not every business must appoint a DPO; where none is required, a contact for privacy requests still is.

title: California opt-out links
question: Does the home page carry the opt-out links California prescribes for businesses that sell or share personal information?
method: Found when the home page links "Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information", "Your Privacy Choices" or "Your California Privacy Choices" (or shows the opt-out icon), or "Limit the Use of My Sensitive Personal Information"; review otherwise, because businesses under the thresholds, or that neither sell nor share data, need no link. Runs when the store appears to sell in the United States.

title: Global Privacy Control declared
question: Does the store declare that it honours Global Privacy Control?
method: GET /.well-known/gpc.json. Found when it is valid JSON with "gpc": true, or the privacy notice mentions Global Privacy Control or opt-out preference signals; review when gpc.json says false or neither is present. Whether GPC is actually honoured happens in the browser and cannot be checked without running JavaScript.

title: No advertising cookies or trackers before consent
question: Does the first response set advertising or analytics cookies, or load trackers without a consent block?
method: Read Set-Cookie on the home page response and the static HTML. Review when the server sets a known advertising cookie (`_fbp`, `_gcl_au`, `IDE`, `fr` and the like) before any interaction, or a known analytics cookie (`_ga` and the like) or when tracker tags (Google tag, Meta pixel, TikTok, LinkedIn, Hotjar and the like) load without a consent-blocking attribute or a denied Consent Mode default; found (none seen) otherwise. Most trackers load through JavaScript, so a clean result means none were seen, never that consent works.

spec.title: UK Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations 2003, regulation 6
